2027-06-12.title: Saturday of the third week after Pentecost
readings: My heart's desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved
If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, nothing will be impossible for you
2027-06-12.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Third Sunday after Pentecost. Tomorrow, the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost, the faithful are reminded of the Apostles' Fast, which begins on Wednesday 16 June.
2027-06-12.verse: For truly I tell you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.
theo: The Epistle opens with one of the most moving sentences St Paul ever wrote: “Brothers and sisters, my heart's desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved.” He is speaking of his own people, the people of Israel. A chapter earlier he has said that he would wish himself cut off from Christ for their sake, and he has listed with pride what belongs to them: the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the worship, the promises, the patriarchs, and, according to the flesh, the Messiah himself. Paul never stopped being a son of Israel, and he never stopped loving his people. When he says, “I can testify that they have a zeal for God, but it is not enlightened,” he is not sneering; he is remembering his own past, when his zeal had made him a persecutor. The Church has learned from Paul to speak of the Jewish people with reverence and gratitude. The Second Vatican Council, recalling these very chapters of Romans, teaches that the Jews remain most dear to God because of their fathers, for the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable (Nostra Aetate 4). No Christian may speak of them with contempt.

Then Paul gives the heart of his Gospel: “For, being ignorant of the righteousness that comes from God, and seeking to establish their own, they have not submitted to God's righteousness. For Christ is the end of the law so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes.” The word “end” here means both the finishing point and the goal, as the finishing line is the end of a race. Our Malayalam Bible renders it: Christ has fulfilled the law. The whole law was running towards him. This is a warning for us, not for others. It is very possible to be zealous for God and still to be trying to establish our own righteousness: to fast, pray, give and serve as a way of being someone in God's eyes and in the parish's eyes. In a few days we begin the Apostles' Fast. Paul tells us in advance how to keep it: not to establish our own righteousness, but to submit to God's, receiving from Christ what we could never make ourselves.

The Gospel brings us down from the mountain of the Transfiguration into a crowd and a family in distress. A father kneels before Jesus: “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is an epileptic and he suffers terribly; he often falls into the fire and often into the water. And I brought him to your disciples, but they could not cure him.” Every parent who has sat up at night with a sick child, or watched a son or daughter fall into the fire and the water of addiction, depression or bad company, knows this prayer. Jesus heals the boy at once. When the disciples ask privately why they had failed, he answers: “Because of your little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move; and nothing will be impossible for you.” Many ancient manuscripts add a further verse, printed as a footnote in our English Bible: this kind goes out only by prayer and fasting. Whatever its place in the text, the Church has always heard in this Gospel a call to the faith that prays and fasts. St John Chrysostom, preaching on this passage, remarked that the mustard seed looks small but is the most powerful of seeds; so faith, small to look at, carries the power of God within it (Homilies on Matthew 57, in substance). On this Saturday, let parents bring their children to Jesus by name, and let all of us ask for the small, real faith that moves mountains.
outline: Ask: for whom is my heart's desire and prayer to God that they may be saved?
Point 1 · Paul's heart for his people
Love, reverence and gratitude for Israel; the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
Christ is the end of the law; do not establish your own righteousness.
Point 3 · Faith the size of a mustard seed
A father's prayer, the disciples' failure, and the faith that prays and fasts.
“If you have faith the size of a mustard seed … nothing will be impossible for you.”
live: Write down the names of three people whose salvation is your heart's desire, and pray for them by name every day of the Apostles' Fast.
Parents and grandparents: tonight, lay your hand on the head of each child or grandchild and pray: Lord, have mercy on my son, on my daughter.
2027-06-12.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you are the end of the law and the righteousness of all who believe. Give us Paul's heart, full of love and prayer for others, and keep us from every contempt for the people of the covenant, to whom your gifts and calling remain. Take from us the zeal that seeks to establish our own righteousness, and teach us to receive everything from you. Have mercy on our sons and daughters who fall into the fire and the water; heal them and bring them home. Give us faith the size of a mustard seed, and as the Apostles' Fast draws near, teach us to pray and to fast with humble hearts. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbono is the righteousness of God given, not earned: Christ, the end of the law, offers himself for us, and the smallest faith that receives him receives the power that moves mountains.

quick: Paul's heart's desire and prayer is that his own people, Israel, may be saved; he loves them and honours their zeal for God.
He teaches that Christ is the end of the law, so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes.
Jesus heals a suffering boy whose father begged for mercy, and tells the disciples that faith the size of a mustard seed can move mountains.
2027-06-12.action: Name three people tonight whose salvation you desire, and begin praying for them daily.
2027-06-12.question: Am I trying to establish my own righteousness, even in my prayers and fasting?

family.explain: A father had a son who was very sick; the boy often fell into the fire or into the water. The father knelt before Jesus and said: Lord, have mercy on my son. Jesus healed the boy. Then Jesus told his friends that even a very little faith, as small as a mustard seed, can do great things, because God is great. Next Wednesday our Church begins the Apostles' Fast, a time of praying and fasting together.
family.intention: We pray for children who are sick, and for parents who are worried about their children.
family.ask: Ask: “What is a mountain in our family that we can bring to Jesus with faith?”

illus: A mother in Kottayam had a son who began drinking heavily after he lost his job in the Gulf. For three years he would disappear for days. She did not stop him by arguing; she had tried that. Instead, every Saturday she took the bus to a nearby church, sat for an hour before the tabernacle and prayed the father's prayer from today's Gospel: Lord, have mercy on my son. In the Apostles' Fast of the third year she added a small fast of her own, giving up her afternoon tea and putting the money in a box for a de-addiction centre. Some months later her son walked into that same centre on his own. She told the counsellor: my faith was very small, smaller than a mustard seed. But I brought him to Jesus every week.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, have mercy on our sons and daughters. Give us faith the size of a mustard seed, and prepare us to pray and fast in the Apostles' Fast. Amen.
share: My heart's desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved (Romans 10:1). Who is the person I most long to see saved?
They have a zeal for God, but it is not enlightened (Romans 10:2). Where is my zeal for God mixed with my own pride?
Lord, have mercy on my son (Matthew 17:15). Which child, young person or family do I want to bring to Jesus today?
interc: For the Church, that she may love all people with the heart of St Paul and pray for the salvation of all.
For the Jewish people, the people of the covenant, that God may bless them and that Christians and Jews may grow in respect and friendship.
For children and young people who suffer in body or mind, and for those caught in addiction, that Jesus may heal them.
For parents who are worried about their children, that their faith may not fail.
For our parish as we prepare to begin the Apostles' Fast on Wednesday, that it may be a time of humble prayer and fasting.
pm.close: Father, Christ is the end of the law and the righteousness of all who believe. Give us Paul's love for others and the father's trust in your Son, and let our faith, small as a mustard seed, bear fruit in prayer, fasting and love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul begins today with words from his heart: Brothers and sisters, my heart's desire and prayer to God for them is that they may be saved (Romans 10:1). He is speaking of his own people, Israel. Paul loved them all his life, and the Church teaches us to speak of the Jewish people with reverence and gratitude, for the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.

Paul says that some had a zeal for God, but it is not enlightened (Romans 10:2). They were trying to establish their own righteousness. That danger is ours too. We can pray and fast and serve to make ourselves important. But Christ is the end of the law so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes (Romans 10:4). We receive righteousness from him.

In the Gospel a father kneels before Jesus: Lord, have mercy on my son (Matthew 17:15). The disciples could not heal the boy, but Jesus did. Then Jesus tells them: if you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move (Matthew 17:20). A small faith, a real faith, is enough, because God is great.

Next Wednesday we begin the Apostles' Fast. Let us keep it humbly, not to make ourselves righteous, but to open our hearts to Christ. Let us bring our children and our families to Jesus by name, and pray for the salvation of those we love. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever seen a mustard seed? It is tiny, smaller than a grain of rice! Jesus said that if we have faith even as small as a mustard seed, God can do great things through us. In the Gospel a father brought his sick son to Jesus, and Jesus made him well. When someone in your family is sick or sad, bring them to Jesus in your prayers. Your faith may be small, but God is very big!

intro: Theme: “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed … nothing will be impossible for you.”
On Saturday of the third week after Pentecost, on the eve of the announcement of the Apostles' Fast: Paul's heart for his people, Christ the end of the law, and the faith that prays and fasts.

sub: “My heart's desire and prayer to God for them.”
q: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem
for the gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
points.apply: Pray this week for the Jewish people and for peace in the Holy Land, and refuse to repeat any joke or remark that shows contempt for any people.

points.h: Christ, the end of the law
sub: How to keep the Apostles' Fast.
q: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts
Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.
points.apply: Before the fast begins, decide on one practice and tell no one but God about it.

points.h: Faith the size of a mustard seed
sub: The faith that prays and fasts.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
points.apply: Bring one person in your family to Jesus by name every day of the Apostles' Fast.

concl: Paul teaches us to love and pray for others, and to receive righteousness from Christ rather than build our own.
A small, real faith that prays and fasts can move the mountains that weigh on our families.
2027-06-12.resolve: Name those whose salvation you desire, and begin the Apostles' Fast with humble, persevering faith.
